# Symbiknow performance evidence

The recorded measurements exercise real EmbeddingGemma 2, Docling and local storage on a small synthetic corpus. They are useful runtime evidence; they do not establish capacity or accuracy for a production library.

Symbiknow / Validation / Performance evidence

## Recorded workload

The benchmark used five files and four questions on an Apple M5 Pro with 48 GB RAM. The measured embedding runtime was MPS with 768-dimensional vectors. Warm model load was 4.01 seconds and process peak RSS was approximately 4,887 MiB. Expected files appeared in the top three for all four questions; exact-file top-one coverage was two of four because Markdown, image and PDF fixtures shared content.

The MCP smoke check recorded verified original bytes, a direct Jev evidence judgment, and a single observed evaluated-search duration of approximately 0.539 seconds. The image check ranked a red image above a blue image using native image vectors without OCR/captions. These observations are not latency percentiles or broad quality estimates.

## Complete source records

The following records preserve the repository artifacts as JSON inside a searchable Markdown document. The numerical source records were generated by the earlier runtime checks; they are not new measurements from this documentation import.

## Reproduction and scope

The source programs are `scripts/benchmark.py`, `scripts/check-mcp.py` and `scripts/check-runtime.py`. They use isolated synthetic repositories or inputs. Runtime checks may invoke the configured hosted Jev API. Keep tests, provider credentials and the live data directory distinct.

Large-corpus indexing throughput, p50/p95 latency, 100,000-document behavior, 16 GB M4 operation, NVIDIA L4 operation, broad OCR quality and power-loss behavior still require separate validation. See `VALIDATION.md` for the complete record.

## Review 9 local retrieval contention

New evidence is under `outputs/mcp-review-9-fixes/`. The before source is preserved with hashes. Local performance fixtures use actual rocfl and LanceDB, 28 independent documents (24 retrieved candidates and four relationship targets), fixed fixture vectors, full detail and a controlled provider replay that seeds eight cached judgments. This isolates local work; it is not a hosted-model or production-capacity benchmark. Each mode has three warmups, 30 sequential samples and 30 barrier-started pairs (60 overlapping request samples). Provider work, embedding time, lock waits/holds and candidate/relationship/final head checks are separate request-local metrics.

Candidate head reads now run outside `INDEX_LOCK`, after grouping passages and sorting the bounded pool. Only candidates that can fill the requested result window are checked. Public search defers preliminary relationship reads to authoritative final publication; other `find_documents` callers retain validated link behavior. Context assembly revalidates the derived revision and returns a restart error on concurrent changes rather than spinning. Final lock order remains server write lock → server index lock → LanceDB index lock → cross-process storage snapshot. Final heads are reused only inside that protected snapshot; current scopes, relationships and retrieved/evaluated windows are checked again after provider latency. Adjacent context and final reference/window validation each use one bounded LanceDB passage read of exact document/version/evidence tuples (maximum 2,000); the protected index/storage snapshot still excludes writers during publication. This batches derived passage reads, never OCFL inventories or authoritative heads.

The unchanged isolated eight-document fixture still requires **16** head reads. The 28-document linked fixture falls from 36–40 reads to **20**: eight candidate heads, eight authoritative result heads, and four final relationship-target heads. This is not a universal 16-read claim. Broad 62-document continuation validates the entire retained window on every page to detect commit/publication gaps, adding bounded local validation cost while avoiding repeated embeddings/retrieval/provider evaluation. Individual window lookups initially raised first-page/continuation observations to 6.62/3.24 seconds; the final bounded passage batches reduced the same isolated 62-match query to 3.47/1.65 seconds. Those single HTTP observations are not percentiles or a general speed guarantee; both raw builds remain saved.

The final bounded-batch benchmark (`benchmark-interleaved-batch.json`) reports overlapping cached hybrid median **531 ms → 176 ms**, p95 **588 ms → 211 ms**, and max **596 ms → 238 ms**. Sequential median is **292 ms → 119 ms**. All 30 paired overlap observations improve; paired uncertainty estimates and every raw sample remain in the JSON. Keyword overlap median is 512 ms → 174 ms; semantic overlap is 446 ms → 167 ms. Earlier intermediate runs are retained, including the explicitly invalid imported-lock run. The benchmark includes the final batched retrieval/freshness algorithm; subsequent changes add initial-lock/model-load timing fields and the compact serialization guard/reserve, which do not alter the full-detail workload measured here. Final HTTP source hashes are in `delivery-http/summary.json`. That final HTTP run observed 1.92 seconds for the first broad page and 0.98 seconds for continuation, with the same 62-match two-page window; earlier single observations of 3.47/1.65 seconds also remain saved. Those observations show machine/process variability and are not percentile estimates. Model context comparisons and HTTP receipts separately record fresh provider request/token usage and cache hits. Document-scoped Jev uses up to eight requests rather than one large batch, increasing fresh-provider latency/cost on this fixture; cached/continuation requests make no new provider calls. No general subsecond, SLA, 16 GB or 100k-document claim follows from these measurements.

The combined handoff rerun is retained separately under `outputs/review9-combined-fixes/retrieval/`. It compares preserved original review-9 source with current retrieval code on a new 28-document isolated corpus, alternating before/after ordering with three warmups, 30 sequential observations and 30 pairs per retrieval mode. Ordinary concurrent verification load was present; fixed vectors and controlled cached provider decisions isolate local cost rather than model inference. Hybrid overlap median/p95/max were **642/1,064/1,299 ms → 226/284/420 ms**; sequential median was **374 → 158 ms**. All 30 paired overlap observations improved for each of keyword, semantic and hybrid. Hybrid paired median improvement was 398 ms, with a deterministic bootstrap interval of 391–415 ms. Raw samples, timing stages and the paired analysis are retained. Current head counts were 19 for keyword/semantic and 20 for hybrid because the selected eight results reached three or four unique linked targets respectively; the eight-document unlinked safety bound remains 16. This reproduces the existing optimization; the new cursor comparison repair changes continuation correctness rather than this full-detail workload.

The new continuation regressions retain four failing before outcomes and four passing after outcomes. They cover in-place final refresh, extracted-text changes without an advanced document head or derived revision, and relationship-target update/deletion before derived publication. Refresh now compares against the retained original window instead of the mutated working copy. Actual HTTP SDK traversal uses a separate 100-document synthetic corpus without a worker or hosted calls, retains all requested 0/1/8/10/62/100 windows, and separately records compact structured and complete SDK byte sizes. This is transport/freshness evidence, not a model-quality or live-library benchmark.

## Later runtime measurements — 17 October 2026

The JSON records above are historical observations and retain their original corpus/scope. Current resource results are documented in `Optimize-memory-symbiknow.md`, `docs/memory-runtime.md` and `outputs/memory-research/followup/`. On the tested Apple M5 Pro/48-GB host, the matched server-plus-children peak fell from 6.06 to 3.98 GiB. Matched warm median was 186 ms unquantized versus 174 ms INT8, while idle reload was 417 versus 641 ms. Final live idle was 720 MiB and dense scanned-PDF peak was 5.00 GiB. Do not add overlapping GPU and process memory counters or generalize these scopes into capacity/accuracy certification.
